title: Gemini API keys are retained across cross-origin redirects
summary: KCS sends Gemini embedding requests with a reusable provider credential in the custom x-goog-api-key header through top-level ureq::post. The pinned ureq 2.12.1 default agent follows 301/302/303 redirects, reuses the header vector, and strips only content-length, cookie, and authorization, so the custom provider credential can be sent to a cross-origin redirect target.
confidence: high (0.96) for header retention; medium for real-world redirect occurrence

codeEvidence.label: Gemini secret resolution
codeEvidence.explanation: The embedding credential is resolved from the declared embedding auth or GEMINI_API_KEY before the outbound request is built.

codeEvidence.label: Credential attached to top-level ureq POST
codeEvidence.explanation: KCS places the credential in a provider-specific header and delegates redirect handling to the top-level ureq request without a KCS redirect policy.

codeEvidence.label: Top-level ureq POST uses default agent
codeEvidence.explanation: The top-level helper constructs a default agent, so the request inherits the default redirect behavior selected by the dependency.

codeEvidence.label: Default ureq agent follows redirects
codeEvidence.explanation: The default agent follows redirects rather than returning the initial 3xx response to KCS for origin validation.

codeEvidence.label: Redirect reconstruction keeps custom credential headers
codeEvidence.explanation: The redirect target is joined without a same-origin requirement, and the header filter strips standard credentials but not x-goog-api-key.

rootCause.summary: KCS treats the initial Gemini URL as the only credential boundary, while the selected HTTP client can replace the final origin after a remote 301/302/303 response. Because the reusable credential is stored in x-goog-api-key and the ureq redirect filter does not classify that header as sensitive, the credential remains on the redirected request.

validation.method: V10 exact repository-to-locked-dependency redirect trace plus local static regression probe
validation.summary: The saved validation traces production embedding execution into a top-level ureq::post carrying x-goog-api-key, confirms Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1, and verifies that the selected redirect code keeps the custom header across 301/302/303 origin changes.
assertions: Normal adopted embedding reaches a default ureq request carrying x-goog-api-key.
The inspected redirect implementation is the dependency version pinned by the repository.
Redirect reconstruction strips content-length, cookie, and authorization, but not x-goog-api-key.
KCS performs no post-redirect origin or scheme comparison before the redirected send.
limitations: No two-origin loopback capture was run.
No open redirect or cross-origin redirect was established at the default Google endpoint.

attackPath.summary: An operator-approved embedding request sends x-goog-api-key to an accepted origin. If that origin returns a cross-origin 301, 302, or 303, ureq rewrites the POST to a bodyless GET, retains the custom credential header, and sends it to the redirect target.

dataflow.summary: resolved embedding credential -> KCS x-goog-api-key header -> top-level ureq::post -> default redirect loop -> redirected request headers
dataflow.sink: redirected request to the Location origin
dataflow.outcome: the Gemini credential crosses from the approved origin to a second origin

reachability.summary: Requires a valid credential, per-adapter network opt-in, an operator-driven embedding operation, and a qualifying 301/302/303 from the accepted origin.
reachability.attacker: accepted origin, compromised service, misconfigured endpoint, or relevant intermediary that can emit the redirect response
reachability.entrypoint: remote Location header on the Gemini embedding request

impact.why: A reusable Gemini credential can be disclosed to an origin that was not approved to receive it.

likelihood.why: The redirect behavior is deterministic, but a qualifying redirect from the default endpoint was not proven.

limitations: HTTPS prevents ordinary on-path redirect injection for the initial request.
The POST body is emptied on the proven 301/302/303 route, so this instance proves credential disclosure, not embedding-text forwarding.

remediation.summary: Disable automatic redirects for credential-bearing Gemini requests, or implement KCS-owned redirect handling that permits only approved same-origin, non-downgrade targets and reconstructs provider credentials after validation.
regressionTests: Static test fails if gemini_embedding.rs uses top-level redirect-following ureq::post with x-goog-api-key.
Two-loopback test returns a 302 from the first origin and asserts the second origin never receives x-goog-api-key.
Same-origin redirect test, if redirects remain supported, verifies credential reconstruction only after policy approval.
307/308 regression ensures future wrapper changes do not replay body plus credential across origins.
